guideIntro: A practical guide for youth workers and administrators. Use the quick-start steps, then jump to the area you need.
guideWorkerIntro: Run a session, keep players moving, and handle day-to-day operations.
guideAdminIntro: Configure the programme, manage access, games, rewards and themes.
guideStep1Body: Check today’s programme, open Attendance and display the staff QR. Players can scan the same QR; each person can record attendance once per day.
guideStep2Body: Use Games to check assignments and help players launch their available activities. Completed games are scored by the server and can recover after a temporary connection loss.
guideStep3Body: Use Assign points for staff-awarded XP. Review public feedback requests before approving them.
guideStep4Body: Review attendance, recent XP activity and follow-up items. Use Notifications for important updates.
guideAdminSetupBody: Set programme configuration, create groups and accounts, configure games, skills and rewards, then review the public display.
guideAccountsBody: Create accounts with the appropriate role, revoke access when needed, and manage group membership. Historical records remain available when access is retired.
guideGamesBody: Use the game library as the starting point. Select a game to edit it, then assign it to young people or groups. Revoke or reassign from the selected game’s assignment panel.
guideAttendanceBody: Generate a fresh staff QR for the session. It refreshes automatically before expiry. The same active QR can be used by multiple players.
guideRewardsBody: Configure scratch-card rewards, stock and skill milestones. Keep descriptions clear so staff and young people know what to expect.
guideThemeBody: Admins can save their own theme presets, use an existing preset, or edit the colour variables. Theme changes apply across the product surfaces.
guideOfflineBody: Completed game and drawing submissions use a durable offline queue. If the browser closes before the network returns, queued work remains available and is retried when the user returns.
guideSecurityBody: Never share staff credentials. Use each person’s own account, revoke access when someone leaves the programme, and use the audit history when investigating changes.
guideNeedHelpBody: If something does not behave as expected, capture the page, action, approximate time and error message before contacting the programme administrator.
privacyIntro: Youth Quest processes personal information to provide the programme service. The organisation running your Youth Quest programme is responsible for deciding the purposes, lawful bases and retention periods for that processing.
privacyDataBody: Depending on the features enabled, this can include account and contact details, gamertag, group membership, attendance, game activity, XP, rewards, skills, drawings, notifications, audit records and technical information needed to operate and secure the service.
privacyPurposeBody: To provide accounts, run programme activities, record attendance and progress, award points and rewards, provide programme administration, maintain security and support the service.
privacySharingBody: Information should only be shared with the organisation’s authorised staff and service providers where needed to operate Youth Quest or where required by law. The programme operator should document its actual processors and any international transfers.
privacyRetentionBody: Retention periods depend on the programme operator and its legal and operational requirements. The operator should publish the actual periods or the criteria used to determine them.
privacyRightsBody: Depending on the circumstances, people may have rights including access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and data portability. The applicable rights depend on the lawful basis and circumstances.
privacyContactBody: Replace this section with the programme operator’s legal name, postal address, privacy contact or DPO details where applicable, and complaint route before production use.
privacyNoticeNote: This page is product guidance, not a substitute for the programme operator’s final legal privacy notice. The operator must complete the organisation-specific details before launch.
cookiesIntro: Youth Quest uses browser storage and cookies to keep the service secure and to provide requested app features such as sign-in, preferences and offline recovery.
cookiesEssentialBody: Authentication/session cookies, security tokens and functional browser storage are used to provide the service, keep accounts secure and support requested features. These are not used for advertising.
cookiesOptionalBody: Do not add analytics, advertising or other non-essential tracking without first assessing the applicable rules and adding an appropriate consent mechanism.
cookiesCurrentBody: Youth Quest does not need a cookie-consent banner solely for essential cookies and strictly necessary storage. If non-essential cookies or similar tracking are introduced, the consent design must be updated before release.
cookiesNoticeNote: The exact technologies used in a deployment should be reviewed before launch, including third-party services and any analytics or marketing tools.

guideWorkerWorkflowIntro: Use these end-to-end checklists when you are carrying out a task from start to finish.
guideWorkerCreateGameBody: Open Games, choose Create game, enter the title, instructions, game type and scoring, save it, then assign it to a young person or group. Open the assignment to check its status, help the player start, and review the completed result.
guideWorkerRemovePointsBody: Open Assign points, choose Remove points, select one young person or a group, enter the amount and a reason, review the confirmation, then submit. Check the activity result afterwards so the correction is recorded.
guideWorkerAwardPointsBody: Open Assign points, select a young person, several young people or a group, enter the XP amount and reason, then submit. If the programme requires approval, the request is sent to an admin for review.
guideWorkerAttendanceBody: Open Attendance, generate the staff QR, display it to the group and let each young person scan it. The QR refreshes automatically before expiry and each person can record attendance once per day.
guideAdminWorkflowIntro: Admins can use these sequences as a practical runbook for setting up and operating a programme.
guideAdminSetupProgrammeBody: Create or review the programme instance, create youth worker and player accounts, create groups, configure skills and rewards, then review the public display before inviting people to use the system.
guideAdminGameWorkflow: Create, assign and manage a game
guideAdminGameWorkflowBody: Open Games, create the reusable game, save its content and scoring, select the game from the library, assign it to a group or individual players, then use the assignment panel to edit, reassign or revoke access as the lifecycle changes.
guideAdminPointsWorkflowBody: Open Assign points to inspect staff awards and pending approval requests. Review the reason and recipient, approve or reject requests where required, and use the activity or audit views to confirm the resulting change.
guideAdminThemeWorkflowBody: Open Theme, choose an existing preset or edit the colour variables, preview the result, save your own preset, then apply it. Keep contrast and readability intact across dashboards, forms and mobile screens.
guideAdminAccountsWorkflowBody: Open People & groups, create the account with the correct role, add group membership where appropriate, use the account card for access changes, and revoke or delete access when the person leaves. Historical programme records remain preserved.
guideAdminRewardsWorkflowBody: Create the reward or skill configuration, set its description and availability, assign it to the intended people or groups, and check the resulting player-facing progress or reward state.
guideCommonTroubleshootingBody: When an action fails, first check the page status and notification, confirm the recipient or assignment, retry once if the network is available, and then check the relevant activity or audit history. Game and drawing submissions can remain queued during temporary network loss.
